What the Bank of England’s Oracle spend teaches us about transformation risk 💡"
""
"The Bank of England has tripled its projected spend on its Oracle cloud migration—from an initial £7M estimate to £21.5M—as contract scope expanded and implementation methodology shifted.  "
""
"Version 1  was originally engaged to support both the technical rollout and change management of the Oracle Cloud implementation. But as requirements grew and additional services were scoped in, the Bank amended its existing contract rather than running a supplier competition, citing interoperability, economic and technical constraints, and the very real cost and disruption of onboarding a new provider mid-project.  "
""
"Here’s what corporate leaders should take away from this:"
"✅ Scope evolves in large-scale transformations, especially in finance stack modernization."
"✅ Mid-project supplier changes aren’t just a contractual swap, they come with integration risks, knowledge gaps, and duplication of work."
"✅ Vendor continuity can be justifiable when specialist domain knowledge is critical."
""
"But there’s also a cautionary angle:"
"⚠️Budgetary deviation naturally raises questions around initial scoping, governance controls, and change-control discipline."
"⚠️ Investing in better upfront requirements and stronger internal capability can materially reduce reliance on contract amendments later."

"Break work down into small, clear, specific deliverables."
"Be realistic about cost (not trying to fit into existing budget target)."

Let me share experience of using Jira in corporate environment."
" "
"Last year me and my team started actively using Jira to manage tasks. Haleon was determined to go Agile and a my whole team went through Scrum Inc. certification (which is helpful)."
" "
"1️⃣ Initially we were using Kanban methodology and what I noticed is that tasks were just hanging in progress status for months."
"Later we switched to Scrum and what I noticed is that some tasks embarked on a never-ending journey, traveling from sprint to sprint."
"💡Conclusion: No matter what methodology you use, there are tasks which will last for ages. The most important for you is to notice them"
"and take actions."
" "
"2️⃣ As a service organization we are making use of ServiceNow so we"
"faced a dilemma on what to reflect in Jira and not to duplicate effort already"
"reflected in SNOW."
"We started with one offs, which were not triggered by incidents (e.g. renew SSL) and project related tasks however eventually significantly reduced project related tasks to avoid double work in Jira and SNOW. "
"Later we started tracking regular activities (e.g. Check-In with vendor), finally we added a single story (worth a single point) for BAU to enable people to speak of what they are working on in case no other stories are assigned to them."
"💡Conclusion: you should create tasks to the extent where it makes sense and be reasonable not to have a situation where Jira administration becomes your major effort."
" "

"1️⃣ If you want to save money, it is time to monitor performance of mid- and senior- managers more closely and "
